title: Import CFMMC futures daily or monthly statements
summary: Import several CFMMC files together and restore fills, cash flows, and positions carried between months.
outcome: You will review futures fills, fees, cash flows, and positions by trading day, and open chart review for matched contracts.
before: Have the daily or monthly statement files obtained from China Futures Market Monitoring Center.
You can select several files at once. Keep their dates continuous where possible.
Reports can contain sensitive account information. Process them only on your own computer.

sections.title: 1. Prepare the CFMMC files
sections.body:
If the files are already on your computer, collect the daily or monthly reports you need. Do not manually change their worksheet structure.

You can also open the CFMMC download page from the online window in TradeReplay. Enter usernames, passwords, verification codes, and two-factor authentication yourself. The tutorial and the app do not record them.

media.label: CFMMC import sources: local files and the online window
media.alt: TradeReplay CFMMC import page with local-file and online access options

callout.title: Complete sensitive steps yourself
callout.body: Never include passwords, verification codes, or identity details in tutorial screenshots or support requests.

steps.title: Open account import
steps.body: Go to Review → Accounts → Import and choose CFMMC.

steps.title: Select the files
steps.body: You can select several daily or monthly reports. TradeReplay parses and groups them by trading day.

steps.title: Wait for every file
steps.body: Do not close the window while a larger batch is being processed. Wait until the file and trading-day counts in the preview stop changing.

media.label: Select several CFMMC files and finish parsing
media.alt: Video showing multiple CFMMC reports selected and parsed in TradeReplay

sections.title: 3. Check the preview

media.label: CFMMC preview with trading days, fills, fees, positions, and cash flows
media.alt: TradeReplay CFMMC import preview showing reports, trades, fees, open positions, and cash flows

sections.body:
Review the file count, trading days, fill count, realized profit and loss, fees, open positions, deposits, withdrawals, and credit entries.

When a monthly statement includes a position carried from the previous month, TradeReplay estimates its opening price from the available settlement and profit data. Gaps in dates or fields may require manual verification.

sections.title: 4. Match futures-contract market data
sections.body:
TradeReplay prioritizes the specific delivery contract instead of substituting only a continuous contract. If local data is missing, follow the prompt to download the relevant contract.

A 9999 continuous contract is useful for continuous observation. For fill-by-fill statement review, use the specific contract that was actually traded whenever possible.

callout.title: Do not identify a contract by its product name alone
callout.body: Delivery months for the same product have different prices and liquidity. Positions carried across months require particular care.

sections.title: 5. Import and check the account

media.label: Calendar and trades after a CFMMC account import
media.alt: TradeReplay account page showing the calendar and futures trades imported from CFMMC

sections.body:
Start the import after confirming the preview. Then use the account details to inspect its calendar, equity curve, instruments, cash flows, and archived statements.

Spot-check one close-today fill, one close-previous-day fill, and one carried position. Confirm direction, price, fee, and opening date.

success: The file, trading-day, and fill counts agree with the statements.
Cash flows distinguish deposits, withdrawals, and credit entries.
Matched contracts open a trade chart and carried positions have verifiable opening details.

faq.q: Can daily and monthly reports be imported together?
faq.a: Yes. Check overlapping dates and duplicate ranges in the preview first. Appending removes duplicates, but you should still confirm the final new-item count.

faq.q: Why is the close-today fee much higher than the close-previous-day fee?
faq.a: Some exchanges and products apply a separate close-today rate. TradeReplay records open, close-previous-day, and close-today fees separately, so one uniform rate cannot explain every fill.

faq.q: Why is the opening price of a carried position different from what I remember?
faq.a: The app estimates it from available settlement and profit data. If an intermediate report is missing or the broker uses a special convention, verify it against the original statement.
